prerequisites: Basic knowledge acquired during high school.

learning_outcomes.text: Develop analytical capabilities and rigorous logical thinking through the study of linear algebra.
Assimilate or fluently handle the main concepts of linear algebra: vector spaces, linear transformations, matrices, determinants, and systems of equations.
Model simple situations and apply appropriate techniques for solving the linear problem posed.
Use exact and approximate mathematical techniques in solving Linear Algebra problems: systems of equations, calculation of eigenvalues, etc.
Understanding and interpreting texts and data, developing skills for their concretization and clear and succinct exposition.
Aptitude for the distribution of resources and time and their implementation in real situations.
Ability to transmit concepts, ideas, processes, etc., related to Industrial Engineering orally and in writing, clearly and correctly.
Ability to use scientific-technical tools for solving calculation and design problems in Industrial Engineering and aptitude for seeking sustainable engineering solutions.
Ability for teamwork and ability for the development of multidisciplinary projects.
Ability to relate to other people and an open aptitude towards creating new relationships.
Aptitude for professional insertion in diverse environments and with varied functions in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Ability to incorporate new knowledge in the area of Industrial Engineering, based on acquired training and necessary for the evolution of technique.
Development of autonomy and creativity, enhancing aptitudes for developing one's own initiatives and undertaking new projects.

Ability to solve mathematical problems that may arise in engineering. Aptitude to apply knowledge about: linear algebra; geometry; differential geometry; differential and integral calculus; differential and partial differential equations; numerical methods; numerical algorithms; statistics and optimization.

syllabus_topics: Introduction. Number representation on the computer. Errors.
Matrices and determinants. Solution of linear equation systems.
Generating sets. Linear dependence and independence. Dimensions and bases.
Definition of linear transformation. Examples. Kernel and image of a linear transformation. Dimension formula. Isomorphisms.
Matrix of a linear transformation with respect to a basis. Change of basis. Rank of a matrix. Calculation of the inverse matrix.
LU decomposition and application to matrix inversion.
Scalar product. Euclidean vector space. Norm of vectors. Angle between two vectors.
Orthogonality of a Euclidean space. Orthonormal bases.
Eigenvalues and eigenvectors of an endomorphism. Characteristic polynomial.
